newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt says won't widen media review.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt says won't widen media review.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it would not widen its media industry review to include foreign ownership.
"The terms of reference have been set," Communications Minister Richard Alston told reporters.
"We've made it clear that it will need to take account of the foreign ownership regime, but it is principally about cross-media and it alway has been."
Canadian media baron Conrad Black said on Wednesday he wanted to lift his stake in newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd to 50 percent from his current 25 percent.
However, Australia's current media rules prevent foreigners from holding more than 25 percent of a newspaper group and more than 15 percent of a television company.
They also prevent a newspaper group owner from holding more than 15 percent of a television station in the same city and vice-versa.
Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said earlier on Thursday he currently saw no need to change the foreign ownership limits.
Black said he would sell out of Fairfax if there was no easing in the current rules, which he described as "anachronistic".

"Ultimately, Mr Black makes his own commercial judgments on these matters," Alston said. "I think he also recognises that from everyone's point of view it probably makes sense to await the outcome of the cross-media review."
Australian billionaire Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd owns 15 percent of Fairfax and has said it would like to merge with Fairfax if the rules were liberalised.
